summary.problem: Gemini CLI automatically maps and shares the entire local `.venv` directory (and other ignored directories) inside custom skills regardless of `.gitignore` or `.geminiignore` rules.
summary.root_cause: In `activate-skill.ts`, `getFolderStructure(path.dirname(skillLocation))` was being invoked without passing a `fileService` option. Without a `fileService`, the utility does not apply `.gitignore` or `.geminiignore` filtering and only falls back to a minimal set of hardcodedignored folders.
summary.context: Other parts of the system, like the workspace folder structure builders in `environmentContext.ts`, properly pass `{ fileService: config.getFileService() }` to ensure ignored patterns are respected.

steps: Locate the invocation of `getFolderStructure(path.dirname(skillLocation))` inside the `ActivateSkillToolInvocation` class.
Pass `{ fileService: this.config.getFileService() }` as the second argument to the `getFolderStructure` function call to enable `.gitignore` and `.geminiignore` parsing.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: When custom skills are activated, standard ignored paths such as `.venv` are not shared with the model.
verification_steps: Add a unit test verifying that `ActivateSkillTool` calls `getFolderStructure` with the `fileService` retrieved from the config object.
Assert that `getFolderStructure` is called with the skill path and an options object containing `fileService: mockFileService`.

github_metadata.title: GEMINI CLI aggressively scans .venv in custom skills (ignores .gitignore / .geminiignore)
